tests.description: Timed check on Space Exploration & Missions

questions.question: Q: What was Sputnik 1 and why was it significant?
questions.correctAnswer: The first artificial satellite, launched by the USSR on 4 October 1957. It marked the beginning of the Space Age and the Space Race.

questions.question: Q: Name three key achievements of the Apollo programme.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) First humans on the Moon (Apollo 11, 1969). 2) Brought back lunar samples for analysis. 3) Demonstrated long-duration spaceflight and lunar operations.

questions.question: Q: What is the ISS and what is its purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: The International Space Station — a habitable satellite in low Earth orbit, continuously occupied since 2000. It serves as a microgravity research laboratory and tests systems for future deep-space missions.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Space Exploration & Missions

questions.question: Q: Why were the Voyager missions significant?
questions.correctAnswer: Voyager 1 and 2 (launched 1977) used gravity assists to visit all four gas giants. Voyager 1 is now the most distant human-made object, in interstellar space. They carry the Golden Record with sounds and images of Earth.

questions.question: Q: What is a gravity assist and why is it used?
questions.correctAnswer: Using a planet's gravitational field to change a spacecraft's velocity and trajectory without using fuel. It allows missions to reach distant targets that would otherwise require too much propellant.
